content.text: I'll answer this from pretrained knowledge of the Andreeva et al. 2008 SCOP paper and the SCOP 1.69, 1.73/1.75 and SCOPe lineages, without reading any file or network source.

answers.answer:
Summary: the relationship was upgraded from a fold-level (analogous, structure-only) relationship in SCOP 1.69 to a superfamily-level (probable homology) relationship, and that reclassification has been carried forward unchanged into the current SCOPe release.

SCOP 1.69: PA1492, the hypothetical protein from Pseudomonas aeruginosa solved by structural genomics (PDB 1t1j, domain d1t1ja_), was placed in the flavodoxin-like fold (c.23; 3 layers a/b/a, parallel 5-stranded sheet, order 21345) but in its own separate superfamily ('PA1492-like'), while nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from Lactobacillus (PDB 1f8y, d1f8ya_) sat in the Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase superfamily (c.23.12, family c.23.12.1). Being in the same fold but different superfamilies meant SCOP asserted only shared topology, i.e. an analogous or unproven relationship, with no claim of common ancestry.

SCOP 1.73/1.75 (the release described by Andreeva et al. 2008): the curators re-examined 1t1j after more detailed structure comparison and analysis of conserved, putative active-site features (including the catalytic nucleophile position of the deoxyribosyltransferases) and concluded that PA1492 and NDT share a common ancestor. The PA1492 superfamily was dissolved and 1t1j was moved into the NDT superfamily c.23.12 as a new, distinct family (c.23.12.2, 'Hypothetical protein PA1492'), alongside family c.23.12.1 (NDT proper, containing 1f8y). The paper uses this as an example of how new data and reanalysis can convert a fold-level relationship into a superfamily-level one, and of how this changes the SCOP hierarchy (merging superfamilies) rather than just adding entries.

Current SCOPe (2.08 lineage, which inherits SCOP 1.75 manual curation): d1t1ja_ remains in c.23.12.2 and d1f8ya_ in c.23.12.1, both under superfamily c.23.12 in fold c.23, class c (alpha/beta). So in the current release the two are classified as homologous at superfamily level but not close enough in sequence/function to share a family.

Evolutionary strength and limits: family = clear sequence-detectable homology; superfamily = probable common ancestry inferred from structure plus functional/active-site features despite low sequence identity; fold = shared topology only, possibly convergent. PA1492 and NDT are now related at superfamily, not family, level, so (1) NDT enzymatic function (nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase activity) must not be transferred to PA1492 without biochemical evidence; PA1492 is still annotated as a hypothetical protein and may have a different substrate or activity; (2) 1f8y is a reasonable remote template for fold-level modelling of PA1492 homologs but residue-level or active-site transfer needs experimental support (enzyme assays, ligand-bound structures) or independent sequence evidence such as profile/HMM searches linking the two families; (3) because each family had only one or few PDB entries, ASTRAL representative selection at 40%/95% identity will keep 1t1j and 1f8y as separate representatives, so a representative-level analysis of c.23.12 should include both. Specific sunids/release-version details are recalled from pretrained knowledge and were not verified against the SCOPe site under this condition.
